heroHeadline: RUTTE MEETS UKRAINE FM SYBIHA AT NATO HQ — ALLIED EUROPE IN EMERGENCY PRE-HELSINGBORG PREP; EU FAC DEFENCE MAY 12; POLAND PUSHES 5% BY 2030; NORWAY SURPASSES US IN PER-CAPITA DEFENSE SPENDING
heroSubtitle: On May 11, 2026, NATO Secretary General Rutte met Ukrainian FM Sybiha at NATO HQ Brussels — the first senior alliance-Ukraine contact following Rasmussen's 'disintegrating' declaration (May 9) — as allied governments formally mobilized for two consecutive crisis sessions: the EU Foreign Affairs Council (Defence) on May 12 and the Helsingborg NATO Foreign Ministers Meeting (May 21–22). Poland raised the stakes by calling for the NATO 5% GDP target to be achieved by 2030 (not the agreed 2035), backed by Estonia, Lithuania, and Latvia. Norway became the first European NATO member to surpass the United States in per-capita defense spending — statistically inverting the burden-sharing argument deployed since 2014. The Helsingborg ministerial is now configured as an emergency session with four agenda clusters: Ukraine support sustainability post-US troop reduction; 5% GDP pathways; Rota/Aviano succession planning; and Rasmussen's coalition of the willing proposal. The EU FAC Defence (May 12) addresses Article 42.7 operationalization (mandated at the April 24 Cyprus summit) and EU military readiness. Background: May 10 — formal allied contingency planning; May 9 — Rasmussen 'disintegrating', Trump Poland transfer 'possible'; May 8 — 'Something fundamental has broken' (Daalder); May 7 — 'terror incubators' CT strategy; May 5 — Tomahawk cancellation; May 1 — 5,000 from Germany. Next: Helsingborg FMM May 21–22, 2026 (first NATO ministerial on Swedish soil); Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8.
